label: DISTANCE

cover.headline: Feeling like roommates? *5 gentle ways back*
cover.sub: For when you run a household together and little else.

points.heading: Name it kindly
points.body: He may be feeling it, too. Saying it out loud, without blame, can be a relief for both of you.
points.panel: “We’ve turned into great co-managers. I miss us.”

points.heading: Bring back one ritual
points.body: Think of something you used to do together and let slip. Start with the easiest one.
points.panel: Coffee together before the day starts.

points.heading: Talk about something else
points.body: Give yourselves fifteen minutes with no logistics. No calendar, no kids’ schedules, no bills.
points.panel: “No house talk for fifteen minutes. Deal?”

points.heading: Touch in passing
points.body: A hand on his back as you walk by. Small contact says “I see you” without a conversation.
points.panel: One small touch today, just because.

points.heading: Plan one thing to look forward to
points.body: It doesn’t need to be big. It needs to be on the calendar.
points.panel: “Let’s pick a night this month that’s just for us.”

close.save: Save this for a busy season.

caption:
You split the chores, coordinate the calendar, and say goodnight. The household runs. The two of you barely overlap.

It can happen quietly, and it can happen to couples who love each other. The way back doesn’t need a grand gesture. A few small ones, repeated, are a good place to start.

Save this for a busy season, and follow @spotseason for more.
